clue.text: In which contenders who've knocked out several others are matched

definitions.text: In which contenders who've knocked out several others are matched

blocks.clueFragment: contenders who've knocked out several others
blocks.note: surface reading: boxers or fighters who have floored several opponents

blocks.clueFragment: In which contenders who've knocked out several others are matched
blocks.note: setter's reading: the last game of a knockout tournament, between the two teams that have eliminated everyone else

explanation.surface: Fighters who have knocked out several opponents are paired up in a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked out' suggests boxing, but here it means eliminated from a knockout competition; the two survivors meet in the last match.
explanation.definitionFit: The climactic match of a knockout tournament such as the FA Cup is played between the two sides left after every earlier round.

clue.text: Person sharing the bill, getting fruit, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a costard is a large old English variety of cooking apple

explanation.surface: An actor sharing top billing who is handed some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a restaurant bill but is a theatre poster's billing.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star is an actor billed alongside another leading performer.

clue.text: One on board making consumer's position clear

definitions.text: One on board making consumer's position clear

blocks.clueFragment: One on board making consumer's position clear
blocks.note: surface reading: a company director explaining where customers stand

blocks.clueFragment: on board making consumer's position clear
blocks.note: setter's reading: a small card on a dining table showing each diner where to sit

explanation.surface: A board member clarifying the position of consumers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' is a dining table and the consumer is someone eating, not a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A small named card set on a dinner table to show each guest the seat assigned to them.

clue.text: In dramatic epic, key equipment used by mountaineer

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

blocks.note: the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: In a dramatic adventure film, a vital piece of a climber's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers on ice and snow use a small pointed axe to cut holds and steady themselves.

clue.text: Starts off paper by foolishly copying others

indicators.note: the starts of the next words are taken off, leaving each without its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plagiarism, starting with a paper produced by mindless copying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' looks like the beginning of an action, but it tells you to remove the first letters of the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Apery is apish behaviour, the silly mimicry of others like a monkey.

clue.text: European city cut by conflict

blocks.note: a conflict between nations
to saw is to cut, as with a blade

explanation.surface: A European city split apart by war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut by' reads as divided by, but 'by' just places the conflict next to the cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital of Poland, a major city in central Europe.

clue.text: Old style of trade-off by company

indicators.note: off as in gone bad or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
Co is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned approach to trade-offs made by a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trade-off' looks like one compound word, but the hyphen hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is the decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s, now a period style.

clue.text: City given another name when burnt

blocks.clueFragment: City given another name when burnt
blocks.note: surface reading: a town renamed after being burned down
setter's reading: add another N, for name, and the city becomes the brown pigment sold as burnt sienna

explanation.surface: A city renamed after a great fire.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name; the Tuscan city plus one more N gives the earth pigment, which artists buy raw or burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Siena is a historic Tuscan city, from whose earth the pigment sienna takes its name.

clue.text: Leave the field, having moderate result in match

blocks.note: having a thing is being with it
a tied game, neither win nor loss

explanation.surface: A team quits the pitch after a so-so result in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave the field' sounds like a sports team going off, but it is the military sense of pulling back troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to retreat or pull out, as an army does from a battlefield.

clue.text: Herb and another fellow are in town

blocks.note: basil is a culinary herb
a don is a university fellow; 'another' because Herb is also a man's name

explanation.surface: Two men, Herb and another chap, are in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Basildon is a new town in Essex, east of London. Herb looks like a man's name, which is why the next fellow is 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Basildon is a large town in Essex, built as one of England's post-war new towns.

clue.text: Us government organisation, say, to retire workers ahead of time

blocks.note: to state is to say
to retire is to withdraw or leave
men are workers, as in a workforce
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A US government body sending its staff into early retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire workers ahead of time' sounds like early retirement; it is three pieces in a row, with the workers placed ahead of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Department is the American federal department that handles foreign affairs.

clue.text: Being agreeable, welcoming bridge opponents in friendship

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: amity is friendly relations
in bridge, East and North sit in opposing partnerships

explanation.surface: Friendly people warmly greeting their rivals at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: AM(EN)ITY: the bridge players are compass points, and East and North are on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenity in its older sense means pleasantness or agreeableness of manner or situation.

clue.text: Island where I come ashore again?

blocks.note: taken as written
the prefix re- means again
a ship's passengers land when they come ashore

explanation.surface: A traveller names the island where they will make landfall once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read in the order I, again, come ashore, so the clue words are rearranged to I re-land.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is the large island to the west of Great Britain.

clue.text: Space behind house that could do for dray

blocks.note: surface reading: a garden area big enough to park a brewer's cart
setter's reading: split the answer in two, and the first word tells you to write the second backwards, which spells the cart's name

explanation.surface: A yard behind a house big enough to hold a brewer's dray.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a set of instructions: take a word for an enclosure and run it back to front to get dray, a low cart for heavy loads such as beer barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A backyard is the open area at the rear of a house.

clue.text: A cold office in church - that's nice!

definitions.note: adjective for a noun: nice in its old sense of exact, the quality being precision

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the office or post held by a curate

explanation.surface: Someone pleased to land a chilly church job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's nice!' sounds like a pleased exclamation; nice here means finely exact, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its old sense means precise or finely discriminating, and precision is exactness or correctness.

clue.text: This board carries out each step by both spirit and letter

definitions.text: This board carries out each step by both spirit and letter

blocks.clueFragment: carries out each step by both spirit and letter
blocks.note: surface reading: a committee that obeys the rules in both their letter and their spirit

blocks.clueFragment: This board carries out each step by both spirit and letter
blocks.note: setter's reading: a board used at seances, where a spirit is said to move a pointer from letter to letter

explanation.surface: A conscientious board of directors that follows the rules to the letter and in spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a committee, but it is a lettered board used to summon spirits; its name joins the French and German words for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used in seances, on which spirits are supposed to spell out messages.

clue.text: Very rude about being broke

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped around another

blocks.note: insolent means rudely disrespectful
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone extremely rude about their lack of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very rude' reads as one phrase, but very is just a letter set inside the word for rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay one's debts, which is what being broke is.

clue.text: Examination requiring no mental effort?

blocks.note: first meaning: a medical check-up of the body
second meaning: bodily, involving the body rather than the mind

explanation.surface: A test that needs no brainwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that an exam you need not think for is really a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical check-up is often called a physical, and physical work is bodily labour rather than mental.

clue.text: Here received characters ending life always?

definitions.text: Here received characters ending life always?

blocks.note: surface reading: an inscription, such as an epitaph, marking where a life ends

blocks.clueFragment: Here received characters ending life always?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the place in Greek myth where everyone who dies is taken in

explanation.surface: A puzzling line about letters that always mark the end of a life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests letters, but it means people: everyone whose life ends is received in this underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the underworld of Greek mythology, the realm of the dead to which all souls go.

clue.text: Chief Superintendent somehow putting up with Morse

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the word's letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: super is the everyday short form of a police superintendent
the opening of the detective's name, shortened

explanation.surface: A senior police officer tolerating Inspector Morse, the TV detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief Superintendent' looks like one rank, but Chief is the definition. Morse is the Oxford detective of the TV series Inspector Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, the boss of an organisation.

clue.text: Rough ocean - it's liable to capsize one

indicators.note: rough water is churned and tossed, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: A rough sea is liable to tip a small boat over.
explanation.walkthrough: On the surface the sea capsizes someone; cryptically the definition is the person liable to capsize.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler in a small open boat, who is prone to overturning in rough water.

clue.text: Show in the same place briefly interrupting former success

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: ex means former
ibid, short for Latin ibidem, means in the same place, and is further shortened to ib
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A brief appearance in the same venue that broke up an old success.
explanation.walkthrough: EX HIT is broken by IB; ib. and ibid. are footnote abbreviations for in the same place.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit is to show or display, and as a noun an exhibit is a show piece.

clue.text: Middleman financially ruined king

blocks.note: broke means having no money
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An agent who has bankrupted a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is an agent who arranges deals between buyers and sellers for a fee.

clue.text: Fish that will quickly bite

blocks.note: first meaning: a reddish food fish of warm seas
second meaning: something that snaps, such as a dog or a turtle

explanation.surface: A fish that bites at the bait quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a family of sea fish and also anything that snaps its jaws shut suddenly.

clue.text: Allow to enter commercial American university

blocks.note: a commercial is an advertisement
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A US university letting in students on commercial terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' looks like an adjective but is a noun, the TV kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, as through a door or into a college.

clue.text: Learner winning at chess very quickly

definitions.text: Learner winning at chess very quickly

blocks.clueFragment: Learner winning at chess very quickly
blocks.note: surface reading: a novice who wins chess games fast
setter's reading: the four-move checkmate named after this kind of learner

explanation.surface: A beginner who wins chess games remarkably fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Scholar's mate is the quick four-move checkmate that catches beginners.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a student or learner, and the fastest common chess win, scholar's mate, carries the name.

clue.text: Narrow miss smoothly faced after this?

blocks.note: first meaning: a near thing, as in a close one
second meaning: the razor treatment that leaves a man's cheeks smooth

explanation.surface: After a near miss, someone faces it out calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoothly faced' sounds like handling something coolly, but it is literally a smooth face.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is a narrow escape, and a shave with a razor leaves the face smooth.

clue.text: In which ads appear to offer business opportunity

blocks.note: first meaning: the interval in a television programme given over to advertisements
second meaning: a lucky chance in trade

explanation.surface: An advertising slot that offers a company a chance to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the TV interval for adverts, and read literally it is a lucky opening in trade.

clue.text: Not oil, but different liquid applied to body

indicators.note: something different is changed, so the letters before it are put into a changed order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Not an oil but some other liquid to rub on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a thin cream or liquid rubbed onto the skin for medicine or cosmetics.

clue.text: He was willing to benefit others by his death

definitions.text: He was willing to benefit others by his death

blocks.clueFragment: He was willing to benefit others by his death
blocks.note: surface reading: a self-sacrificing hero ready to die for others
setter's reading: making a will, so that others inherit when he dies

explanation.surface: A selfless man ready to give his life for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' sounds like eager, but it means drawing up a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is the person who has made a legal will leaving property to heirs.
